analysis.title: Tech selloff highlights rising scrutiny of AI spending (UBS House View - CIO Alert)
key_insights: US tech led stocks lower on Friday 10/30. Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on the day and 2.0% on the week. S&P 500 fell 1.8% on the day and 0.6% on the week. The 10-year Treasury yield fell 1bp on Friday and 7bps on the week to 4.93%.
Brent crude rose further this week to USD 118/bbl on concerns the US may resume military strikes against Iran, adding to risk-off sentiment.

UBS says 3Q earnings show AI infrastructure demand remains exceptionally strong, but the market reaction reflects a shift in the AI debate. Earnings expectations are broadly met, and investors now weight overinvestment, financing and cannibalization concerns more heavily.

Overinvestment: Alphabet kept its USD 195-205bn 2026 capex plan, reported negative free cash flow for the quarter and signalled a significant further capex increase for 2027. Shares fell almost 13% the next day.

Overinvestment: Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex range to USD 135-145bn and pledged continued aggressive investment beyond 2026. Shares fell nearly 7% the next day on the higher capex floor and negative 3Q free cash flow.

Cloud growth, the key gauge of return on AI spending, is accelerating. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y (82% prior quarter, 34% in the March quarter). Azure grew 48% (43% in the June quarter). Oracle cloud growth quickened to 62% from 47%. All three guided to further cloud growth, saying added capacity could serve pipeline demand.
Microsoft reported an eight-fold increase in large Copilot accounts. Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users.

Financing: neocloud credit (providers that mainly rent GPU compute capacity) has sold off on a maturity and funding mismatch. Large upfront debt-financed investment is supported by later cash flows that depend on utilisation, execution, customer renewal and refinancing.

UBS estimates neoclouds are about 8% of its capex estimate versus 80% for Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and SpaceX. UBS expects selective project delays, repricing and consolidation rather than a broad collapse in AI spending.
Cannibalization: Alphabet Search query growth hit a five-year high but Search revenue growth decelerated, as management said AI Mode monetizes at a lower rate.
Intel fell 28.6% on Friday. AI is lifting server orders but also causing component scarcity, so Intel could not fully meet data center demand, and higher PC prices are hurting its client business.
UBS raised aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027, and introduced USD 1.5tr for 2028.

UBS expects higher volatility in the AI trade to be the new normal. It would grow concerned if AI-lab revenue growth slows meaningfully, cloud utilization weakens, or falling AI costs fail to stimulate enough new usage to absorb capacity.

UBS would also reassess its spending outlook if algorithmic efficiency sharply cuts compute needs, if larger investments fail to bring matching capability gains, or if worsening financial conditions limit even hyperscalers' willingness to fund investment.

Positioning advice: reduce overconcentration across the AI value chain, preferring foundry, compute and power names with reasonable valuations and less excess-capacity risk. Rebalance across sectors and asset classes, favoring industrials, health care, financials, the Eurozone, EM, Asia ex-Japan and high-quality fixed income. Use volatility deliberately, with predefined entry prices.

earnings_insights: Alphabet 3Q (reported): maintained 2026 capex plan of USD 195-205bn, negative quarterly free cash flow, significant further capex increase signalled for 2027. Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y vs +82% prior quarter. Shares fell almost 13% the following day.
Meta 3Q (reported): lower end of 2026 capex range raised to USD 135-145bn, negative 3Q free cash flow. Shares fell nearly 7% the following day.
Microsoft fiscal 1Q (reported, three months to September): Azure +48% vs +43% for the June quarter. Large Copilot accounts up eight-fold.
Oracle (reported): cloud growth +62% vs +47% prior period.
Intel (reported): shares fell 28.6% on Friday. Server orders rising, but component scarcity limited data center supply and higher PC prices hurt the client business.
UBS says earnings expectations are broadly being met across the season.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell 1bp on Friday and 7bps on the week as quality bonds rallied while stocks fell.
Rose further on concerns the US may resume military strikes against Iran, weighing on risk sentiment.
Raised forecasts supported by stronger spending commitments from the largest hyperscalers.

risk_factors: Overinvestment: rising capex floors and negative free cash flow at Alphabet and Meta.
Financing: neocloud credit stress from maturity and funding mismatch, with sensitivity to utilisation, execution, renewal and refinancing.
Cannibalization: AI Mode monetizes below traditional Search, and component scarcity pressures PC prices and Intel's client business.
Slowing AI-lab revenue growth, weaker cloud utilization, or falling AI costs failing to spur enough new usage.
Algorithmic efficiency gains sharply reducing compute requirements.
A significant deterioration in financial conditions constraining hyperscalers' willingness to fund investment.
US-Iran military escalation and high oil prices (Brent USD 118/bbl).
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects higher volatility in the AI trade to be the new normal at this stage of the cycle.

UBS advises investors to use volatility deliberately: prepare in advance, and use swings to rebalance, manage downside risk, generate income or build exposure gradually at predefined prices. Structured strategies carry issuer, liquidity, pricing and capital-loss risks.
UBS flags elevated single-stock risk after earnings and advises diversifying across the AI value chain.
Quality bonds rallied this week as stocks fell. UBS says elevated yields cushion against future bond market volatility.
geopolitical: Concerns that the US may resume military strikes against Iran pushed Brent crude to USD 118/bbl.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth is accelerating (Google Cloud +103%, Azure +48%, Oracle +62%), advance orders for compute are expanding, and UBS raised AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex floors are rising with negative free cash flow at Alphabet and Meta, neocloud credit is stressed, and AI is cannibalizing Search monetization. Alphabet fell almost 13% and Meta nearly 7% after results.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slowing AI-lab revenue growth, weakening cloud utilization, or falling AI costs failing to stimulate enough new usage to absorb expanding capacity.
